relevance_note: The paper describes a family with three HA20 patients carrying a heterozygous TNFAIP3 missense variant ("identified in three patients from the same family") and summarizes 12 previously reported index cases with TNFAIP3 missense variants in Table 2.
method_note: Read the full paper Markdown, including the supplementary section (Figure 3/4 western-blot and flow-cytometry source data only; no patient-level content). The output was built with a Python script in the scratch directory; table spans were cut programmatically from the Markdown table lines (row label through the person's cell) and every value was checked by hand against Tables 1 and 2; the script asserted that every span occurs verbatim. Table 1 has patients as columns, headed I.1, II.1, II.2 (data columns 1-3). Table 2 has index cases as columns headed by the variant: data column 1 = c.707T>C (current study, = proband II.2, not given a separate row) and data columns 2-13 = c.305A>G, c.386C>T, c.574G>A, c.728G>A, c.824T>C, c.929T>C, c.1129G>A, c.1428G>A, c.1639G>A, c.1804A>T, c.1939A>C, c.2126A>G. Labels: the family members use the paper's labels (I.1, II.1, II.2, I.2). Table 2 index cases have no person label, so rule 3 was applied to columns as 'Table 2 column k' (k counting data columns from the left); their relatives from the 'Family segregation' row are labelled '<relation> of Table 2 column k'. Where the paper names a group without a count of individuals ('Mother and sisters', column 10) two sister rows were made (the minimum implied by the plural; the true number is not stated); 'three other family members' (column 5) became 'other family member 1-3'. Relation words are lower-cased. The label span for literature persons is the column's variant header or the family-segregation cell. Scope: the healthy mother I.2 (tested negative) is included; healthy control donors are out of scope. publications.n_patients_reported and cohort_size_as_stated = 3 (the family's patients as stated); Table 2 adds 12 previously published index cases and 19 relatives, which are not in that count. cites_prior_report_of_same_patients = true refers only to the Table 2 literature cases; the family itself is not said to have been reported before. Not recorded or recorded conservatively: CRP values (I.1 15, II.1 7, II.2 7 mg/L) are not described as elevated, so the CRP/ESR checklist item is 'not reported'; plasma cytokine elevation is a group-level comparison and was not given per-person rows. Inheritance for II.2/II.1 is 'not reported' (father carries the variant and the mother does not, but the paper does not state the parental origin; recorded in parental_testing_statement). Column 6 (Leu275Pro) is called a 'de novo variation' without any description of parental testing, so inheritance is 'not reported' under rule 8. Zygosity is 'not reported' for literature cases (not stated per person). Consanguinity is stated only for II.2. Broad organ-system 'No' cells in Table 1 were used to exclude narrower checklist items (Ocular No -> uveitis/ocular inflammation excluded; Hepatic No -> autoimmune hepatitis excluded; Musculoskeletal No for II.1 -> arthritis or arthralgia excluded); 'Cardiovascular: No' was not used for 'pericarditis or other serositis' or 'vasculitis' (composite or not clearly covered). Table 2 'Ulcers: No' excluded oral and genital ulcers but not the composite GI ulcers-or-inflammation item. 'No'/'Yes' are words, not symbols, so no legend was needed. Relatives' statements 'no symptoms' (columns 7, 13), 'same symptoms' (column 8), 'milder symptoms' (column 9), '(mildly) symptomatic' (column 12) and unspecified 'ulcers' (column 5) were recorded as single feature rows and not mapped to checklist items; 'isolated oral ulcers' was not used to exclude other features. Column 3 'deceased from cerebral hemorrhage' gives a feature row but was not mapped to CNS involvement. Column 3 fever cell reads 'Yes^&'; the '&' footnote is not defined in the paper. Column 11 onset 'Before 32 months' has no ISO duration (upper bound only). Contradictions found: (1) Table 2 Reference row gives 'Chen et al., 2020b' for c.305A>G, while the text and table footnote give 'Chen et al., 2020a' (ref 2020b is the PremPS tool paper). (2) p.(Leu236Pro) is 'of uncertain significance' according to ACMG in the Results text but 'Likely pathogenic' in Table 2, and the text later says its pathogenic significance is demonstrated. (3) p.(Leu275Pro) is 'Pathogenic' in Table 2 but 'the likely pathogenic p.(Leu275Pro) variant' in the text. (4) p.(Thr602Ser) is 'Likely pathogenic' in Table 2 but 'can be considered as pathogenic' in the text. (5) p.(Ile310Thr): Table 2 lists 'Reduced A20 expression' while the text cites 'the absence of functional alteration of the variant'. (6) p.(Thr647Pro): the text says carriers 'lack HA20 hallmark clinical features' while Table 2 lists occasional oral ulcers in the index case and (mildly) symptomatic relatives; the text statement was not used to exclude anything. (7) II.2 colchicine response: 'significant improvement' in the text vs 'Colchicine (partial response)' in Table 2; both are quoted.
